leading_positions.synthesis: Five members state B053 (optical lattice clocks) as their single preferred prize part, all with Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. Shared ground: a magic-wavelength lattice, performance near 1e-18, reproduction and comparison across several laboratories, and a two-name credit that fits the three-person limit. What is not shared: how much weight the 2005 (frequency comb, Ye) and 2012 (ion control and clocks) prizes carry against novelty, whether the pending SI redefinition of the second is a reason to wait, and whether the Sr-lattice priority history is settled. Citation wording differs slightly (invention and realisation, magic-wavelength concept, 10^-18 level). Eriksson and Johansson moved to this position from lower or second places in the opening, and the Chair is also among the supporters, having moved from third place. Alternatives listed differ: B001 (Johansson, Kroll), B016 (Lindroth), B033 and B013 (Eriksson), and B009 and B046 (Pearce).

Danielsson alone prefers B046 (experimental Higgs discovery with ATLAS and CMS), with Gianotti, Della Negra and Virdee. Its case is secure confirmation, significance for the origin of particle mass, and a long wait since the 2013 theory prize. He himself names the attribution as the hardest feature and lists B053 as an alternative. Other members who mention B046 (Eriksson, Johansson, Pearce) accept its importance but cite the allocation among four names and the absence of agreement on which three.

Mehlig alone prefers B013 (topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect), with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, citing a general Z2 mechanism, a first clear experimental realisation in HgTe and fifteen years of independent confirmation. Others rate the science highly (Eriksson, Johansson and Lindroth treat it as a serious alternative or competitor) but object to the attribution, since Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are outside the credited names, and to the 2016 topological-phases prize. Members' triples differ: Eriksson and Olsson would add Hasan in place of Mele, while Mehlig and Johansson keep Mele.

Olsson alone prefers B052 (aberration-corrected electron microscopy), with Rose, Urban and Haider, as an invention in the statutory sense that removed the Scherzer limit and is now routine. Others (Lindroth, Mehlig, Eriksson) describe it as an enabling instrument and ask whether it counts as physics discovery. Olsson herself flags thin opening support, the uncredited STEM corrector work of Krivanek, Dellby and Lupini, and her own proximity as a practising microscopist.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members confirm that B053 is scientifically strong: independent replication at the 1e-18 level across several laboratories, a magic-wavelength lattice that is a recognisable step beyond single-ion clocks, and tests of redshift over millimetres and of varying constants. Five prefer it as their single prize part and Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson name it as an alternative.

Every member who addresses it treats the superconducting-circuit field (B001) as strong science but cautions that it follows closely after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and that Girvin is outside the credited names. Johansson himself moves it below B053 and recommends recusal on it.

Magic-angle graphene (B033) is regarded as important but is described by Eriksson (who withdrew it as his preferred part), Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll and Mehlig as young, with the pairing mechanism unresolved and Cao outside the credited names.
All eight members propose single-part prizes in round 1; none proposes a second part. Johansson and Kroll note that the three-person limit makes most second parts awkward.
Several members (Pearce, Lindroth, Johansson, Eriksson, Olsson) ask for expert reports to check priority history before names are fixed, for the clocks, the Higgs founders, and microscopy.
scientific_disputes: Whether B053 is a distinct step or a third chapter in the precision-metrology line after the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and whether the new physics is the magic-wavelength concept or the engineering path to 1e-18. Kroll and Lindroth argue the former; Olsson, Mehlig and Danielsson press the latter as a reservation, and Danielsson asks what has been learned about nature given that fundamental-physics tests so far are null results.

Whether a measurement-instrument or technique prize (B053, B052) weighs equally with the discovery of a phenomenon or a quantum state of matter (B013, B033), a question Eriksson, Mehlig and Lindroth raise explicitly.
Whether the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions leaves room for B013. Mehlig argues the time-reversal-symmetric Z2 class is distinct; Johansson, Danielsson and Kroll see overlap.

Whether IceCube's diffuse flux is secure and its source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are firm enough, which Danielsson and Pearce question, with Lindroth deferring to astroparticle colleagues.
Whether the TEM aberration corrector is physics rather than chemistry or engineering (B052), raised by Pearce, Eriksson, Lindroth and Mehlig and answered by Olsson on the statutory word invention.
attribution_disputes: B053 has the same two names in every member's proposal (Katori, Ye) and no member disputes the pair, but Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson, Pearce, Eriksson and Johansson each say the Sr-lattice priority history among Tokyo, JILA, SYRTE, PTB and NIST, and contributors such as Lemonde, Ludlow, Hall, Peik and Hollberg, has not been verified from the record.

B046 has four credited names for three places. Danielsson proposes Gianotti, Della Negra and Virdee, Johansson proposes Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, and Pearce's opening list was Gianotti, Jenni and Della Negra. The disagreement is over which founder is omitted, and Danielsson notes that two collaborations of thousands make any trio contestable.

B013 has four credited names for three places and members differ on the triple: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (Mehlig, Johansson) against Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan (Eriksson, Olsson). Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe, and the 3D ARPES strand (Hasan, with Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents) is separable from the 2D quantum spin Hall effect.
B009 allocation among Halzen, Spiering and Karle is open, given the AMANDA and Baikal precursors, as Pearce, Danielsson, Kroll and Lindroth note.
B052 is contested over the uncredited STEM corrector of Krivanek, Dellby and Lupini, which Olsson, Eriksson and Pearce raise.
B033 credit excludes Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, and earlier moire band theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto), as Johansson, Kroll and Danielsson note.
maturity_disputes: Whether the pending redefinition of the SI second is a reason to delay B053. Mehlig and Lindroth (as a qualification) raise it. Kroll, Johansson and Pearce reply that the prize concerns demonstrated performance that is already independently confirmed and that redefinition follows the evidence.
B033 is eight years old with an unsettled pairing mechanism; Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig and Eriksson judge it more likely to age well if the committee waits.
B013 is about fifteen years old, with an uncontested mechanism, which Mehlig and others accept as mature. The doubt is about attribution and about overlap with the 2016 prize, not maturity.
Whether the fourteen-year gap since the Higgs observation makes B046 overdue or whether the 2013 theory prize has already honoured the central discovery.
Whether the IceCube source associations are developed enough, as Pearce, Danielsson and Kroll question.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and works in superconducting circuits at Chalmers, and recommends recusing himself from B001 (circuit QED) and discounting his own ranking of it.

Kroll worked a year in John Hall's JILA laboratory during his PhD, the institution where Jun Ye works. He describes this as a scientific lineage tie, not a collaboration, and flags it for B053. He is also part of the WACQT leadership, overlapping institutionally with Chalmers, and would be more cautious on B001.
Eriksson chaired the 2025 cycle and discloses this as context for B001.
Olsson is a practising electron microscopist at Chalmers and flags proximity to B052; Johansson is a Chalmers colleague with no tie to B052.
Pearce, as Chair, works in astroparticle physics and detector development (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur), adjacent to B009 and with no IceCube affiliation. He has no conflict noted for B053.

Lindroth is a close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and has worked with Lund attosecond and Keller groups, and will be careful on AMO entries B016 and B001. She states no formal recusal for B053.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict. Mehlig notes institutional Gothenburg ties to Johansson and Olsson.
questions_for_round2: For B053, do the expert reports confirm that Katori and Ye are the right and sufficient pair given the Sr-lattice priority history across RIKEN and Tokyo, JILA, SYRTE, PTB and NIST, and what citation wording best isolates the magic-wavelength lattice advance from the 2005 and 2012 prizes?

Does the committee treat the 2005 and 2012 precision-metrology prizes as a reason to decline or defer B053, and can Eriksson, Olsson and Mehlig, who raise it as a reservation or prefer other candidates, say whether it is decisive for them?
Should the pending redefinition of the SI second affect the timing of B053, or is the performance already established, as Kroll, Johansson and Pearce argue?

Mehlig, Danielsson and Olsson prefer B013, B046 and B052 respectively. What would each need to see (a defensible triple, a resolved allocation, a resolved STEM priority question) to move a ballot ahead of B053, and which of the three disputes is likely to be answered by expert reports?
For B046, can any three of Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee be defended in a citation, and is Danielsson's trio, Johansson's trio or Pearce's trio preferable?

For B013, should the citation be restricted to the quantum spin Hall effect so as not to over-credit the prediction, which names go in, and does the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission make any triple unacceptable?
Does the committee prefer a one-part prize on B053 or any second distinct part, given the three-person limit, and if so which candidate and which names?

How should the committee weigh instrumentation or technique prizes (B053, B052) against discovery of a phenomenon (B013, B033, B046, B009), and does the statutory word invention settle the physics-versus-chemistry question for B052?
summary.chair_observation: Five of eight explicit round-1 configurations name B053 with Katori and Ye, while B046, B013 and B052 each have one explicit supporter. Nothing in the files shows how the three members with other first choices would vote if B053 were set aside, and I draw no inference from that. The B053 convergence rests on attribution and reproducibility, but the Chair notes that most of its supporters also share unresolved reservations about overlap with earlier metrology prizes and priority history, and that those points are untested against expert reports. Round 2 should focus on those reservations and on whether the competing configurations can answer their own attribution questions.
